questions.question_text: Identify the correct indirect speech equivalent for the sentence: 'The officer asked the subordinate, 'Why did you not submit your report yesterday?''
options: The officer questioned the subordinate why he didn't submit his report yesterday.
The officer told the subordinate that he did not submit his report the day before.
The officer asked the subordinate why he had not submitted his report the previous day.
The officer had asked the subordinate why he not submitting his report yesterday.
questions.explanation: When converting a 'Why...' question (wh-question) into indirect speech, 'did not' changes to 'had not' (past perfect), and 'yesterday' changes to 'the previous day.'

questions.question_text: Choose the correct indirect speech conversion for the statement: John said to me, "The FIA exam was difficult yesterday, but I passed it."
options: John told me that the FIA exam was difficult the day before, but he had passed it.
John told me that the FIA exam was difficult the day before, but he passed it.
John told me that the FIA exam had been difficult the day before, and he had passed it.
John said me that the FIA exam had been difficult the day before, but I had passed it.
questions.explanation: When reporting speech, the tenses must shift back (Simple Past $ightarrow$ Past Perfect) and time adverbs must change (yesterday $ightarrow$ the day before). Since John is the subject, all pronouns must refer to him ('he had passed it').

questions.question_text: Choose the grammatically correct passive voice transformation of the active sentence: 'The committee members appointed John the Head of Department after a detailed discussion.'
options: After a detailed discussion, John had been appointed the Head of Department by the committee members.
The committee members appointed John to be the Head of Department after a detailed discussion.
John was appointed the Head of Department by the committee members after a detailed discussion.
The Head of Department was appointed John by the committee members after a detailed discussion.
questions.explanation: In passive voice, the direct object (John) becomes the subject, and the original verb structure ('appointed') takes the passive form ('was appointed').

questions.question_text: Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence: "The government is expected to pass the new education policy by next month."
options: The new education policy will be expected to pass by the government next month.
The new education policy was expected to pass by the government next month.
The new education policy is expected to be passed by the government next month.
The new education policy has been expected to pass by the government.
questions.explanation: The structure 'is expected to' indicates a passive construction, requiring the main action to be phrased as 'to be passed' to maintain tense consistency and shift the focus to the policy.

questions.question_text: Which sentence correctly converts the direct speech into indirect speech? He asked the librarian, "Could you please tell me where the Urdu section is?"
options: He asked the librarian if he could tell him about where the Urdu section was.
He asked the librarian whether to tell him where the Urdu section was.
He asked the librarian whether he could tell him about the Urdu section.
He asked the librarian if he could tell him where the Urdu section was.
questions.explanation: Since the direct speech is a request/question using 'Could', we use 'if' (or 'whether'). The interrogative word 'where' acts as the connector, making the structure: 'if' + Subject + could + tell + Object + where... was'.

questions.question_text: The principal was accused of neglecting his duties, but the committee insisted that the faulty policy must be revoked.
options: The principal was accused of neglecting his duties, but the committee insisted that the faulty policy revoke.
The principal was accused of neglecting his duties, but the committee insisted on the revocation of the faulty policy.
The principal was accused of neglecting his duties, but the committee insisted that the faulty policy be revoked.
The principal was accused of neglecting his duties, but the committee insisted that the faulty policy was revoked.
questions.explanation: Verbs like 'insist' require the use of the subjunctive mood after 'that,' which means the dependent clause should use 'that + subject + (be) + base form' (i.e., 'that the faulty policy be revoked').

questions.question_text: Convert the following sentence into Indirect Speech: The Chief Superintendent said to the personnel, "The results of the next round of interviews will be announced on Monday."
options: The Chief Superintendent warned the personnel that the results of the next round of interviews must be announced on Monday.
The Chief Superintendent told the personnel that the results of the next round of interviews had been announced on Monday.
The Chief Superintendent asked the personnel that the results of the next round of interviews will be announced on Monday.
The Chief Superintendent informed the personnel that the results of the next round of interviews would be announced on Monday.
questions.explanation: When 'will' is used in direct speech and the reporting verb is in the past tense, it must shift to 'would' in indirect speech. Since the statement provides general information, using the reporting verb 'informed' is the most appropriate and academic choice.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the following sentence: The committee recommends that all applicants submit their biometric data before the closing date.
options: It is recommended by the committee that all applicants submit their biometric data before the closing date.
All applicants are recommended to submit their biometric data by the committee before the closing date.
The submission of biometric data by all applicants is recommended by the committee before the closing date.
It was recommended by the committee that all applicants submitted their biometric data before the closing date.
questions.explanation: This sentence uses the subjunctive mood structure ('recommend that + subject + base form of the verb'). Since the main verb ('recommends') is in the present tense, the passive structure must maintain the present tense auxiliary, 'It is recommended'.

questions.question_text: Choose the option that correctly converts the following statement into a passive form, retaining the meaning and grammatical structure: 'They recommend that she complete the assignment immediately.'
options: It is recommended by them that she completes the assignment immediately.
It is recommended that she complete the assignment immediately.
The assignment should be completed immediately, recommending her efforts.
That she should complete the assignment immediately is recommended by them.
questions.explanation: The structure 'recommend that + Subject + Base Verb' (subjunctive mood) is best preserved using the impersonal passive structure: 'It is recommended that...' followed by the base verb.

questions.question_text: Choose the option that maintains both the correct tense sequence and the formal tone suitable for an academic exam:
options: While the chairman spoke, the journalist suddenly flashed his camera, interrupting the proceedings.
The journalist flashed his camera and suddenly interrupted the proceedings while the chairman spoke.
While the chairman was speaking, the journalist suddenly flashed his camera and interrupted the proceedings.
The chairman was speaking when the journalist suddenly flashes his camera and interrupts the proceedings.
questions.explanation: The Past Continuous Tense ('was speaking') correctly sets the background action, which is then interrupted by a sudden, single action in the Simple Past Tense ('flashed and interrupted'), establishing correct temporal consistency.

questions.question_text: Identify the sentence that correctly converts the following direct speech into indirect speech: She exclaimed, "How beautiful the view is from this hill!"
options: She exclaimed how beautiful the view was from this hill.
She exclaimed that the view is very beautiful from that hill.
She exclaimed that the view was very beautiful from that hill.
She exclaimed, 'How beautiful the view is from that hill!'
questions.explanation: Exclamatory statements converted to indirect speech typically use a reporting structure (e.g., 'exclaimed that...') and require tense backshift (is to was) and appropriate changes in demonstratives (this to that).

questions.question_text: Which option correctly transforms the active voice sentence, 'The committee must review the proposal before the deadline,' into the passive voice?
options: The proposal must reviewed by the committee before the deadline.
The proposal is having to be reviewed by the committee before the deadline.
By the committee, the proposal must be reviewed before the deadline.
The proposal must be reviewed by the committee before the deadline.
questions.explanation: The structure 'must + be + Past Participle' is required for the modal passive voice. Option B correctly applies this structure, ensuring grammatical accuracy.

questions.question_text: Identify the grammatically correct passive structure for the sentence: 'The committee members will finally approve the new draft guidelines after the arduous deliberation.'
options: The new draft guidelines will finally be approved by the committee members after the arduous deliberation.
After the arduous deliberation, the new draft guidelines will finally approve by the committee members.
By the committee members, the new draft guidelines will finally be approved after the arduous deliberation.
The arduous deliberation will finally approve the new draft guidelines by the committee members.
questions.explanation: The structure is Future Passive ('will be approved') and the prepositional phrase ('by the committee members') can optionally be placed at the end of the sentence for better flow.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct indirect speech rendition for the command: 'The supervisor ordered the staff, 'Finish this report by 5 PM today!''
options: The supervisor commanded the staff to finishing the report by 5 PM that day.
The supervisor ordered the staff that they should finish this report by 5 PM tomorrow.
The supervisor ordered the staff to finish that report by 5 PM that day.
The supervisor told the staff finishing the report by 5 PM today.
questions.explanation: Commands (imperative statements) are reported using an infinitive (to + V1). 'This' changes to 'that', and 'today' changes to 'that day' or 'the next day' to reflect the time shift.

questions.question_text: Choose the most grammatically accurate passive form of the following active sentence: 'The committee might announce the results by the end of the day.'
options: By the end of the day, the results might announce by the committee.
The results were might be announced by the committee by the end of the day.
The results might be announced by the committee by the end of the day.
The announcement of results might be by the committee by the end of the day.
questions.explanation: To form the passive voice with a modal verb (might), the structure is 'Modal + be + Past Participle'.

questions.question_text: Choose the sentence that correctly changes the active voice to the passive voice, maintaining the original meaning and tense:
options: The committee members were discussing the controversial proposal.
The controversial proposal was being discussed by the committee members.
The controversial proposal has been discussed by the committee members.
The committee members discuss the controversial proposal.
questions.explanation: The original sentence is in the Past Continuous Tense (were discussing). The corresponding passive voice structure is 'was/were + being + V3', which is correctly implemented in Option B.

questions.question_text: A student stated, 'Sir, I could not attend the seminar yesterday because I was ill.' How should this statement be reported using indirect speech?
options: The student stated that he could not have attended the seminar the previous day because he was ill.
The student stated that he could not attend the seminar yesterday because he was ill.
The student stated that he could not attend the seminar the previous day because he was ill.
The student stated that he was unable to attend the seminar the day before due to illness.
questions.explanation: When reporting speech, 'could not' remains the same. 'Yesterday' must change to 'the previous day' (or 'the day before'). Option A maintains all necessary backshifts.

questions.question_text: Report the following conversation: Rohit said to Amir, “I finished my assignment yesterday, so I must submit it today.”
options: Rohit told Amir that he had finished his assignment the previous day, so he had to submit it that day.
Rohit told Amir that he finished his assignment the day before, so he had to submit it that day.
Rohit informed Amir that he must finish his assignment the previous day.
Rohit told Amir that he had finished his assignment the day before, so he had to submit it that day.
questions.explanation: The statement requires tense shift. 'Finished' becomes Past Perfect ('had finished'), and 'yesterday' is most formally translated as 'the previous day'. 'Must' shifts to 'had to'.

questions.question_text: Identify the most grammatically accurate indirect speech conversion for the sentence: 'The supervisor exclaimed, 'We must complete this report by tomorrow morning.'
options: The supervisor exclaimed that they had to complete that report by the next morning.
The supervisor exclaimed that they must complete that report by the following morning.
The supervisor exclaimed that they should complete it by the following morning.
The supervisor exclaimed that they must complete this report by tomorrow morning.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, the modal 'must' suggesting obligation changes to 'had to' (or 'would have to'), and time/demonstrative adverbs like 'this' and 'tomorrow' must be shifted to 'that' and 'the following day'/'next morning' respectively.

questions.question_text: Change the following sentence into indirect speech: 'Neither Imran nor his teammates were serious about the match until the coach reminded them that the tournament was crucial.'
options: The coach reminded them that neither Imran nor his teammates had been serious about the match until the tournament was crucial.
The coach had reminded them that neither Imran nor his teammates had been serious about the match until it was crucial.
The coach reminded them that neither Imran nor his teammates were serious about the match until the tournament was crucial.
The coach reminded them that neither Imran nor his teammates were being serious about the match until the tournament was crucial.
questions.explanation: Since the reporting verb ('reminded') is in the past, the tense of the clause ('were serious') must shift to Past Perfect ('had been serious') to reflect the reported time.

questions.question_text: She said, "I finished the entire report yesterday.". Convert this statement into indirect speech.
options: She told her friend that she finished the entire report the day before.
She said that she finished the entire report the previous day.
She said that she finished the entire report yesterday.
She said that she had finished the entire report the previous day.
questions.explanation: The original statement is in Simple Past (finished). In indirect speech, Simple Past shifts to Past Perfect (had finished), and 'yesterday' becomes 'the previous day' or 'the day before'.

questions.question_text: The officer advised the staff members, “Please file the reports immediately and ensure all files are signed.”
options: The officer advised the staff members to filing the reports immediately and ensuring all files were signed.
The officer advised the staff members to file the reports immediately and ensure that all files were signed.
The officer advised the staff members filing the reports immediately and ensuring all files were signed.
The officer asked the staff members to file the reports immediately and ensure all files are signed.
questions.explanation: For reported requests/advice, the structure is 'advised + object + to + infinitive'. Tenses must also be correctly shifted (e.g., 'are signed' to 'were signed').

questions.question_text: If we rearrange the sentence, "The old manuscripts are known by historians worldwide," into an active voice, which option is grammatically correct and natural?
options: The old manuscripts are known by historians worldwide.
Worldwide historians know the old manuscripts.
The world's historians know the old manuscripts.
Historians worldwide know the old manuscripts.
questions.explanation: The original passive sentence implies a general truth. In the active voice, 'Historians worldwide' (plural subject) performing the action 'know' (simple present) is the most direct and grammatically sound option. Option B is also acceptable but A is simpler and less ambiguous.

questions.question_text: The old man said, "Neither the children nor the students were paying attention to the lecture." Which of the following is the correct reported speech equivalent?
options: The old man said that neither the students nor the children were paying attention to the lecture.
The old man said that neither the students nor the children pay attention to the lecture.
The old man told that the students or the children paid attention to the lecture.
The old man reported that the children or the students were paying attention to the lecture.
questions.explanation: The sentence uses 'neither...nor', which remains the primary structure. Since the original statement was in the past continuous ('were paying'), the reported speech must maintain a past tense structure that accurately reflects the original meaning, which Option A does.

questions.question_text: Select the correct indirect speech conversion for the command: The librarian said to the students, "Submit your assignment before Friday."
options: The librarian advised the students to submit their assignment before Friday.
The librarian ordered the students submitting their assignment before Friday.
The librarian told the students that they should submit their assignment before Friday.
The librarian requested the students to having submitted their assignment before Friday.
questions.explanation: Direct commands are best converted using an infinitive structure (to + verb). Using 'advised' or 'requested' conveys the tone appropriate for a librarian and maintains perfect grammar.

questions.question_text: She asked me, "Could you possibly provide me with the necessary documentation for my application?"
options: She asked me if I could possibly provide her with the necessary documentation for her application.
She asked me to possibly provide her with the necessary documentation for her application.
She asked me if I could possibly to provide her with the necessary documentation for her application.
She requested me whether I could possibly providing her with the necessary documentation for her application.
questions.explanation: A polite request starting with 'Could you' is best reported using 'if' (or 'whether') and maintaining the modal structure 'if I could', followed by the correct pronoun changes.

questions.question_text: Convert the following direct speech into indirect speech: The officer commanded the guards, 'Do not allow any unauthorized entry into the secure zone.'
options: The officer told the guards that they should not allow any unauthorized entry.
The officer advised the guards that they must not allow any unauthorized entry.
The officer ordered the guards to not allow any unauthorized entry into the secure zone.
The officer commanded the guards not to allow any unauthorized entry into the secure zone.
questions.explanation: Imperative statements or commands are best converted using infinitive structures ('not to' + base verb) to accurately convey the strong prohibition.

questions.question_text: Identify the correct indirect speech conversion for the sentence: John exclaimed, "What a beautiful view this is!"
options: John exclaimed how beautiful the view was.
John wished that the view to be very beautiful.
John exclaimed that the view was very beautiful.
John wondered that the view was so beautiful.
questions.explanation: Exclamatory sentences expressing strong admiration ('What a...') are best converted using the structure 'exclaimed how... was'. Option B is the most grammatically correct and idiomatic choice.

questions.question_text: Which of the following sentences correctly converts the active voice action into the passive voice?
options: The committee has been reviewing the detailed proposals since morning.
By the committee, the detailed proposals have been reviewed since morning.
The detailed proposals have been being reviewed by the committee.
The detailed proposals were being reviewed by the committee since morning.
questions.explanation: The question is fundamentally flawed as none of the options represent a direct passive conversion. However, Option A is the only grammatically sound sentence structure presented, using the Present Perfect Continuous Active voice, making it the most plausible intended answer despite the faulty premise.

questions.question_text: Choose the sentence that correctly converts the following speech into reported speech: Rohan said to Aisha, "I have completed my report, so I will submit it tomorrow."
options: Rohan told Aisha that he has completed his report, so he will submit it tomorrow.
Rohan told Aisha that he had completed his report and would submit it the next day.
Rohan said to Aisha that he had completed his report, and that he will submit it the next day.
Rohan told Aisha that he would complete his report and submitted it the following day.
questions.explanation: The present perfect ('have completed') must change to past perfect ('had completed'), and 'will' must change to 'would' in reported speech. Additionally, 'tomorrow' must be converted to 'the next day'.

questions.question_text: Identify the sentence that correctly reports the following dialogue: Mary said to John, “If I were you, I would resign because the pay is insufficient.”
options: Mary suggested to John that she should resign because the pay was insufficient.
Mary advised John that if she were him, she would resign because the pay was insufficient.
Mary urged John, advising him to resign due to the inadequate salary.
Mary told John that she might resign since the pay was insufficient.
questions.explanation: When reporting advice using the 'If I were you' structure, the conditional form ('if she were him, she would resign') is maintained, and the tense shift 'is' to 'was' is correctly applied.
